name: Tourist-rental registration and renewal manager for conciergeries and multi-property hosts (API Meublés number tracker)
buyer: Conciergeries (Airbnb management firms), multi-property hosts and small agencies managing tourist rentals; also private hosts with 1-5 units
trigger: Art. L324-1-1 Code du tourisme as applying from 20 May 2026; décrets 2026-196 and 2026-197 of 19 Mar 2026; national teleservice for hosts expected in Q4 2026; the registration expires on a period set by decree (not found) and a transition period applies for old numbers; fines of up to 10,000 EUR cited by one guide, 5,000 EUR by another, so unverified; the number must appear on every listing.
existing: Competitor search (conciergerie plus numero d'enregistrement outil/logiciel) found none. JD2M (jedeclaremonmeuble.com) is a paid LMNP accounting firm that only explains the process and does not file for the host. The state teleservice itself is free. PMS vendors (Smoobu etc.) are not shown to handle registration.
unchecked: The renewal period and fee in décret 2026-196; whether the national service offers bulk or multi-property filing or an API for managers; whether PMS and channel managers (Lodgify, Guesty, Hostaway) will add number tracking; local change-of-use authorisations (e.g. Paris, Lyon) are a second layer. Number of conciergeries not counted.

first_check.duty: Loi n° 2024-1039 (19 Nov 2024) and Art. L324-1-1 Code du tourisme. From 20 May 2026, anyone offering a meublé de tourisme anywhere in France must file a declaration and get a registration number, which must be shown on every listing. Platforms must take down listings that have no number. Décrets 2026-196 and 2026-197 of 19 Mar 2026 are in force. Art. 6 of décret 2026-196 (R.324-2-1 to R.324-2-4) covers data sent by intermediaries and refers to the number's validity and to a declarant who may differ from the host. I did not find the renewal interval. Main-residence status must be proven. Fines: DGE cites up to 5,000 EUR for a missing number. Secondary sources cite up to 10,000 EUR for failing to declare and 20,000 EUR for a false or fraudulent number. I did not check the 10,000 and 20,000 EUR figures in the legal text. The DGE page fetched seems to describe the old commune-by-commune regime.
first_check.market: DGE estimates about 1.2 million meublés de tourisme. Xerfi (Oct 2025) and Pricelabs both cite about 5,000 conciergeries in 2024. This is not an official register count; Sirene by NAF code was not checked.
first_check.competitor: Hostcare: a jotform mandate offers to handle the whole declaration for a flat 39 EUR TTC, for its network of conciergeries. This is a done-for-you filing service that already exists. Smoobu (PMS): its 2026 guide tells hosts to enter the number in the PMS, which syncs it to Airbnb, Booking and the booking engine, so displaying the number is covered. The state teleservice is free (Q4 2026). Platforms check the number themselves. Not checked: whether Lodgify, Hostaway or Guesty support the number, and whether the teleservice will allow bulk filing or have an API for agents. I found no dedicated tool that tracks registrations and renewals across a portfolio.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Under loi 2024-1039 and Art. L324-1-1 Code du tourisme, every tourist rental in France needs a declaration with a registration number from 20 May 2026, and the number must appear on each listing. But the national teleservice is not open yet (DGE says Q4 2026), so its bulk filing, API and agent options cannot be checked. Décret 2026-196 separates the declarant from the host, so filing through an agent looks possible. I did not find the renewal period, so the duty may be close to one-off. Hostcare already files for a flat 39 EUR on behalf of its conciergerie network, and PMS tools like Smoobu store the number and sync it to listings. Fines differ by source (5,000, 10,000 or 20,000 EUR).

challenge_check.killer: No killer found. Closest substitutes: Hostcare's 39 EUR done-for-you filing mandate, the free national teleservice (Q4 2026), and PMS fields for the number (Smoobu). Not settled: the renewal period (set by a decree I did not find), whether the teleservice will allow bulk or agent filing, and whether Lodgify, Hostaway or Superhote support the number.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills the idea, but it is weak. Hostcare files the declaration for 39 EUR TTC per unit under an administrative mandate. Smoobu syncs the number to listings. The state teleservice is free. I found no portfolio tool that tracks registrations or renewals for conciergeries. Décret 2026-196 (R.324-2-4) separates the "déclarant" from the "loueur", so filing by a third party seems possible, which helps the idea. The national teleservice is still not open (planned Q4 2026). The renewal period remains unknown: it is set by a decree I could not find. Without a known renewal cycle, the "recurring" part is unproven. It may come down to one batch of re-filings of old numbers. The PMS vendors could add number tracking easily.
